# Pre-registration: M13b, dense probe of the Garnier interview (follow-up to an M13 observation)

Written 2026-11-28 ~11:50 UTC, before any query with this protocol. The git commit of this file timestamps the plan.

**Why (a hypothesis generated by data, now tested on new queries).** In M13 (claude-opus-4-5-20251101, article
54068170076, *«Nosotros, como el tiempo, también nos desdoblamos»*, 2010, 1,279 FineWeb-2 copies), the window at
word 300 gave the original's next 9 words in all 10 attempts, and 7 of 10 attempts then contained "en el que podemos
hacer cosas cuya", a phrase from word 204 of the same article: neither in the prompt (words 300–409) nor in M13's
scored text (words 410–659). M13's score cannot see matches with other parts of the article. This test asks, with new
queries and a score fixed in advance, whether Claude reproduces this interview's wording more than it does for
comparable unseen interviews.

**Items.** Member: the Garnier interview, text from `data/fw2_top_text.json` (sha256 7f3eef1b…, as in M13).
Controls: the first 4 *La Contra* controls of M13's offset-control list (11458911, 11460053, 11478598, 11479519;
published Feb–Mar 2026, after the training data of both models; 886–924 words, Garnier 901). Same section and format.

**Models.** Primary: `claude-opus-4-5-20251101` (where the pattern was seen; training cutoff Aug 2025). Secondary:
`gemini-3.1-flash-lite` (cutoff Jan 2025).

**Procedure** (`src/m13b_garnier.py`). M13's prompts unchanged (offset 0: M11's prompt; other offsets: M13's
mid-article prompt), title = URL slug as in M13. Windows: a 110-word prefix starting every **50** words, offsets
0, 50, … while at least 50 words follow the prefix (Garnier: 15 windows; controls: 15, 15, 15 and 16). **3 attempts per
window**, one API call each (Claude: default decoding, sampling parameters are rejected by the API; Gemini: attempt 1
at temperature 0, attempts 2–3 at T=0.8, top_p=0.95, seed = article ID + offset + i). 256 output tokens on Claude,
probe.py's floor on Gemini. Every call is an evidence record in `evidence/m13b_garnier/calls.jsonl`.

**Score (fixed now).** Per attempt: the longest common word run between the output and the article text **outside
the prompt window** (words before the prefix and words after it), with M11's normalization; a run is flagged *quote*
if the matched text contains or sits inside quotation marks (M11's rule). Per window: best run outside quotes over the
3 attempts. Per run we also record where in the article it matched, to tell "continues the prompt" from "elsewhere".

**Primary test**, per model: Garnier windows > control windows (best run outside quotes), one-sided Mann–Whitney,
α = 0.05 for Claude (primary); Gemini reported as secondary.
**Secondary:** (a) windows with a run ≥ 12 words (controls reached at most 9–10 in M13); (b) "echoes": windows with a
run ≥ 6 words that matches article text **not adjacent to the prompt** (not starting within the 250 words after the
prefix), Garnier vs controls (Fisher, one-sided).

**Reading.** Garnier above controls (primary), with echoes or long runs: Claude holds part of this interview's
wording, from the article or its many reposts (still La Vanguardia's text). Labelled adversarial (NYT-style prompts)
and as a follow-up of a data-generated hypothesis. The interviewee's own terminology (Garnier's theory has its own
vocabulary, used in his books) is a confound: every run ≥ 12 words, and every echo, is checked against Garnier's
public writings before it is described as the newspaper's wording. No difference: the M13 observation was chance.

**Size and cost.** 76 windows × 3 attempts = 228 calls per model. Claude Opus 4.5: ≈ US$2. Gemini: cents.
